boards.school_name: University of North Carolina School of the Arts
boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented UNCSA spaces for individual work, group work, research, rehearsal preparation, and media study.

cards.title: Library and Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: UNCSA campus library
cards.notes: Start with the public study areas and choose from tables, cubicles, or group spaces based on whether you need solo focus or a shared work surface.
cards.short_summary: The central library offers several publicly described study-space formats.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA’s High School Handbook states that public study space throughout the library includes tables, cubicles, and group spaces.
cards.access_notes: Use the library’s current access and service information before visiting.

cards.title: Library Auditorium
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons, Room 1106
cards.notes: Use this room only when it is unoccupied or scheduled for an appropriate activity; check the library calendar or space-reservation process before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A named library room documented as the Library Auditorium.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA’s library calendar identifies Room 1106 as the Library Auditorium.
cards.access_notes: Availability varies with scheduled events; verify the calendar or reservation requirements.

cards.title: Library Room 2107
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons
cards.notes: Ask the library before relying on this room: the faculty manual lists it for recurring class use and requires library approval before registrar submission.
cards.short_summary: A library room identified for recurring class meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2025–26 UNCSA Faculty Manual lists Room 2107 among library spaces available for recurring classes on a first-come, first-served basis with library approval.
cards.access_notes: Not a drop-in guarantee; obtain library approval for recurring class use.

cards.title: Library Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons, Room 2209
cards.notes: Plan computer-based work here when the room is not scheduled for a workshop; consult the library calendar or staff for current availability and access.
cards.short_summary: A named computer lab inside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA identifies Library Room 2209 as the Computer Lab in its employee learning-and-development schedule.
cards.access_notes: Room use may be affected by scheduled workshops; confirm availability with the library.

cards.title: Library Seminar Room 4209
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons, fourth floor
cards.notes: Use this as a planned group-work option rather than assuming drop-in access; the university lists it among library rooms requiring approval for recurring classes.
cards.short_summary: A named fourth-floor seminar room in the library.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA’s Faculty Manual lists Room 4209 as a library space available for recurring classes, subject to library approval.
cards.access_notes: Approval is required for recurring class use; check scheduling before visiting.

cards.title: Listening & Viewing Room
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons, Room 4210
cards.notes: Bring a defined listening or viewing task and verify that no event is scheduled; the library calendar names this room specifically for listening and viewing.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated media-oriented room in the library.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA’s library calendar identifies Room 4210 as the Listening & Viewing Room.
cards.access_notes: Availability depends on scheduled use; check the current library calendar.

cards.title: Library Self-Taping Room
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons
cards.notes: For a rehearsal or audition-prep session, follow the Drama Art Hub and 25Live process described by UNCSA rather than treating the room as open access.
cards.short_summary: A library room used by drama students for practice and rehearsal.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA’s High School Handbook says drama students use the library self-taping room for regular practice and rehearsal.
cards.access_notes: Practice and rehearsal spaces are reserved through the Drama Art Hub/25Live process described by UNCSA.

cards.title: UNCSA Archives Research Room
cards.subtitle: Third floor, University Library Annex
cards.notes: Schedule an appointment with Archives staff, then bring a laptop or pencil and paper for primary-source work; bags, food, and beverages are not allowed.
cards.short_summary: An appointment-based room for studying UNCSA archival materials.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA Archives says its Research Room is open by appointment to students, faculty, staff, and the public, and is on the third floor of the Library Annex.
cards.source_title: Using the Research Room — UNCSA Archives
cards.access_notes: Appointment required. Archives materials are used only in the Research Room; follow handling and no-food rules.

cards.title: Library Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons, lower level
cards.notes: Confirm current availability with library staff before planning a project session; UNCSA’s emergency guidance identifies the Makerspace on the library’s lower level.
cards.short_summary: A named lower-level library space documented by UNCSA.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA’s emergency-response guidance identifies the Makerspace as a location in the lower level of the Library.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current project-space access and any equipment rules with the Library & Learning Commons.

cards.title: Connector Building
cards.subtitle: Between Moore and Sanford residence halls
cards.notes: If you are eligible to use its study rooms or computer lab, contact the Connector Desk to reserve space instead of assuming a room is available.
cards.short_summary: A high-school-life building with study rooms, a computer lab, and flexible classroom space.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA says the Connector Building houses study rooms, a computer lab, arts studio, flexible classroom space, kitchen, and multipurpose space.
cards.access_notes: UNCSA directs users to contact the Connector Desk to reserve Connector Building space.
